newsitem.title: UK: S&P may still cut BT, may raise MCI.
newsitem.headline: S&P may still cut BT, may raise MCI.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Friday it was keeping British Telcommunications Plc ratings on CreditWatch with negative implications and MCI Communications Corp on watch with positive implications.

BT has AAA senior unsecured and corporate credit ratings while MCI has senior unsecured and corporate ratings of A. They were put on CreditWatch last year after the two groups announced their intention to merge, creating an entity called Concert.

"Upon completion of the merger process and provided that there are no significannt changes in the companies' business and financial profiles in the interim, Standard & Poor's will equalise the rating of the two companies and expects to assign its AA corporate credit rating to the combined entity," it said.
"The companies expect to obtain all the necessary approvals to complete the process before the end of 1997," S&P said.
"The expected downgrade of BT's ratings reflect the company's increased business risk and weakened financial profile resulting from its acquisition of MCI," it said.

"The merger will create one of the most competitive global telecommunications companies with a broad geographic reach, an excellent product portfolio and a well diversified business and customer base," the agency said.
But it added that from a ratings viewpoint, the merger eroded the stability benefits derived from BT's strong position in the British telephony market.

"While MCI has a well established position in the U.S. long distance market, its operations in this industry entail a higher business risk than BT's operations in the UK telecommunications market, where the company certainly enjoys the leading position in most business segments," the statement said.
